content:
maria-plat: starting RL-999 canary on /v1/stream-gen -> ramping to 30% at 14:24 UTC. low risk but tagging infra.
ops-bot: [ROLLOUT] RL-999 started by maria-plat (canary=30%)
lauren: seeing a small uptick in 5xx from the canary cohort, not baseline yet. looks correlated with cache eviction spikes on the KV cluster.
ken: can you confirm which key prefixes? streaming sessions or model-cache?
lauren: mostly session:* and stream-state:* TTL churn. eviction_rate went from 2% -> 18% in 60s.
david_r: if session churn is killing the KV working set, better to cut traffic back immediately. proposal: fast-fallback -> baseline=100, enable kv_protect_mode to stop aggressive evictions, then investigate.
maria-plat: agree. plan: (1) set traffic to baseline, (2) flip kv_protect_mode, (3) avoid full prefix purge unless necessary, (4) collect targeted telemetry for 3m.
anika: flagging support to prep short blurb if streaming connections drop. @support-team
ken: CLI for immediate actions:
```
# revert canary traffic
redwood rollouts set --id RL-999 --traffic "baseline=100,canary=0"
# enable protective kv mode (limits eviction and read-throughbackoff)
redwood feature-flags set kv_protect_mode on --env prod
# pin fallback route to baseline
redwood routing update --route /v1/stream-gen --fallback baseline
```
infra-bot: [ACTION] rollouts-service: set traffic RL-999 -> baseline=100 by maria-plat
maria-plat: executed traffic revert and setting kv_protect_mode now.
infra-bot: [FLAG] kv_protect_mode=on by maria-plat
lauren: watching dashboards: eviction_rate trending down, error_rate decreasing to ~0.9%. tail-latency stable.
david_r: good. hold off on any cache key deletes. if errors re-emerge after 2m, we'll run a targeted cleanup for hot keys only.
ken: targeted cleanup pattern (use carefully):
```
redwood cache hot-list --prefix "session:" --threshold 1000 > /tmp/hot.txt
redwood cache delete --file /tmp/hot.txt
```
lauren: note: deleting session keys will drop a subset of active streams; prefer tombstone+grace if possible.
maria-plat: support message drafted: "We briefly reverted a canary and enabled protective mode to stabilize streaming sessions. Some users may see short reconnects. We're monitoring." sending now.
support-team: confirmed. will triage inbound tickets and escalate if >20m.
ops-bot: [METRIC] post-revert: canary_error_rate 0.8% baseline 0.6%; kv_evictions 3.2% -> 0.4%
anika: next steps / follow-up: create INF-952 with root-cause work and rollout UX improvements.
maria-plat: creating INF-952: items: (a) add canary-scoped KV hit/miss metrics, (b) automatic kv_protect_mode toggle when eviction_rate > 5% sustained, (c) rollout UI: expose "kv guard" checkbox that will auto-enable protective flags during canary
ken: also add an automation: if canary_error_rate p90 > 2% for 1m, automatically roll traffic back to baseline.
lauren: and add a post-deploy canary smoke test that simulates session key churn so we don't regress.
david_r: agreed. scheduling quick postmortem if RC confirmed. thx all for fast action.
maria-plat: closing loop: traffic stayed at baseline, kv_protect_mode left on for 5m then we evaluated. no purge performed. INF-952 created. closing thread.
